POST /api/v1/storage/{id}/update

Update a storage repository

Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. Queues an update after Core's current generation matches expected_generation. A name-only update is metadata-only and preserves the existing credential without reconnecting the backend for non-clustered repositories. A source update uses the full dependency guard. Credential-only rotation is allowed while attached only when every referring VM is shut off and no pending or needs_attention disk, media or ISO work refers to the repository. Generic updates, including a rename, are refused for source.iscsi.mode clustered_gfs2 as a failed Core operation: clustered iSCSI updates require a coordinated Core cluster operation. No coordinated cluster update API exists. Core revalidates source and receipt, journals before native effects, and reports generation/access. If rollback cannot be proven, the result is needs_attention, never a safe failed update. 202 is acceptance, not mount readiness; identical request_id replays and changed input is 409.

POST /api/v1/storage/{id}/detach

Detach a storage repository

Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. Core checks expected_generation and applies the full dependency guard, including VM disks, retained disks, ISO media and pending or needs_attention disk/media work. A successful detach removes only Nex-owned configuration; it never formats or deletes backing data. Generic detach of source.iscsi.mode clustered_gfs2 is a failed Core operation before native commands: clustered iSCSI detach requires a coordinated Core cluster teardown. No coordinated teardown API exists. If side-effect rollback is uncertain, Core reports needs_attention rather than a safe failure. 202 is not proof that unmount completed.

POST /api/v1/networks

Register pool guest network

Administrator session required. Mutations require same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token; JSON rejects unknown fields and bodies over 1 MiB. Persist request_id before sending. Identical payload replays return the same resource/operation; changed payload conflicts. New work requires a fresh active host in the selected pool advertising managed-vm-v1. Poll resource lists and operations for terminal results. HTTP acceptance is not host completion. No disk formatting. kind vlan creates an additive guest bridge on the host without touching the management bridge; other kinds perform no network configuration. For kind vlan the submitted host_id only selects the pool: the registration is master-owned, so the response and later reads carry the pool master as host_id, and resending the identical body (member host_id included) replays the same registration and operation. Unobserved or non-physical uplinks conflict with 409. Definite failed registrations can be revalidated using a new request_id; queued, dispatched and needs_attention reservations must be reconciled first.

DELETE /api/v1/networks/{id}

Remove a pool VLAN guest network

Implemented in development product 0.3.5, protocol v1. Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required; JSON rejects unknown fields and bodies over 1 MiB. Controller only relays: the target host is always the pool master resolved from the pool record, so host_id is not accepted and a body carrying one is refused with 400 invalid JSON request. The pool master's Core checks the expected generation, refuses while any VM on any host in the pool references the network (running or stopped) and while any ready member's published VM inventory is stale, tears the guest bridge, its 802.1Q sub-interface when no other Nex stanza uses it and its /etc/network/interfaces.d stanza down, and journals a durable tombstone. Members converge on their next member pull pass, refusing locally while one of their own VMs uses the network. Only kind vlan networks are removable; a host-automatic bridge or libvirt network is refused with 409. 202 is acceptance, not teardown: the registration disappears from the library only when the master reports the tombstone. An identical request_id replays the same operation with 200; a different body under that request_id is 409. Requires the pool master to advertise pool-resource-removal-v1. Two different answers share this route, decided by what the Controller already holds. On a registration whose operation failed and which no host reports as applied this is a local discard: it takes no body, relays nothing, deletes only the Controller's own request row, audits network.discard and answers 200 {"id", "deleted": true} — a refused registration published nothing on any host, so there is nothing to ask a host to undo. A failed row whose resource a host has since reported as applied is refused with 409 "a host reports this registration as applied, so it is not a failed request record; remove it on the host instead of discarding it". Everything above describes the relayed pool-VLAN removal, which is unchanged for a registration the master reports as applied. PATCH is unchanged too: a failed request record cannot be renamed.

PATCH /api/v1/networks/{id}

Rename a pool VLAN guest network

Implemented in development product 0.3.5, protocol v1. Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. Same relay and same body as the removal plus name, which must be nonblank, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes and free of slashes and control characters. Renaming is the only change this call makes: the bridge name is derived from the uplink and VLAN tag and appears in every VM's domain XML, so changing an uplink or VLAN tag means removing the network and registering a new one, which gives it a new identity. The pool master records the new name at generation + 1 and rewrites its interfaces.d stanza; each member steps its own generation forward on its next pull pass, and a member whose uplink or VLAN differs reports pool network <id> changed uplink or VLAN; remove and re-add it instead of re-plumbing a bridge. Only kind vlan networks can be renamed (409 only pool VLAN networks can be removed). 202 is acceptance; the new name appears when the master reports it.

POST /api/v1/media

Upload and transfer a guest ISO

Administrator session required. Mutations require same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token; JSON rejects unknown fields and bodies over 1 MiB. Persist request_id before sending. Identical payload replays return the same resource/operation; changed payload conflicts. New work requires a fresh active host in the selected pool advertising managed-vm-v1. Poll resource lists and operations for terminal results. HTTP acceptance is not host completion. Send the raw ISO body, not multipart or JSON. Name must be a basename ending .iso. Controller hashes the actual stream, verifies CD001 at offset 32769 and stages privately before committing an iso-import command. There is no fixed per-image maximum: an upload is admitted only while the staging filesystem's free space, less a 256 MiB Controller reserve, covers it; one transfer admission at a time, 2-hour read/write budget. Capacity is bounded even with absent/false Content-Length. Identical retries reupload and hash the bytes before comparing the original request. Terminal import results release Controller staging; orphan files are removed at startup. Use POST /api/v1/media/download to request a public URL import on Core.

POST /api/v1/vms/{id}/console

Issue a single-use console ticket for a running VM

Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Requires an administrator session, same Origin and X-CSRF-Token, and an empty JSON object body. The VM must be an adopted appliance or a successfully created guest, its assigned host must be freshly connected, unrevoked and report capability console-v1, and the VM must be observed running in fresh libvirt inventory. The ticket is bound to the requesting session user and VM, lives 60 seconds in Controller memory only, is delivered once to the host in its next report response and is consumed by the first matching WebSocket. The action is audited as console.open. No power operation is implied; a Controller restart ends open consoles without affecting the guest.

GET /api/v1/vms/{id}/console/{ticket}

Open the browser console WebSocket

Implemented in development product 0.1.0. WebSocket upgrade (RFC 6455, binary frames carrying raw RFB/VNC bytes for noVNC) authenticated by the administrator session cookie; the Origin header must equal the Controller origin and the ticket must be unconsumed, unexpired and issued to this session user for this VM. Controller waits up to 20 seconds for the host's outbound tunnel, then relays bytes both ways until either side closes. HTTP/1.1 is negotiated for this route; no other transport is offered. The ticket is consumed on first use.

POST /api/v1/agent/console/{token}

Attach the host's outbound console tunnel

Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Core sends this over its enrolled, hostname-verified mTLS connection with Connection: Upgrade and Upgrade: nex-console after receiving a console request in a report response and dialing the running VM's local VNC UNIX socket. The token must name an unexpired session for this exact host that has no tunnel yet. The response is 101 and the connection then carries raw VNC bytes both ways until the browser or VM side closes. Other hosts, unknown or expired tokens and duplicate tunnels receive 404. No browser session or CSRF token is used on this agent route; Core never listens for inbound console connections.

GET /api/v1/updates

Check Controller software updates

Implemented in development product 0.1.0. Refreshes a signed Controller-owned APT index cache at most every 5 minutes and reports apt's candidate version for nex-controller against the installed version. The configured repo URL (NEX_UPDATE_REPO or /etc/nex/updates.conf, else https://nexvirtualization.com/apt) is written to that cache and verified with the packaged archive keyring; this keeps the unprivileged Controller service out of the system APT state. A refresh failure or package no configured source offers is returned in the error field with HTTP 200 so operators can still see the installed version. Administrator session required. Read-only; safe to retry.

POST /api/v1/updates/apply

Request Controller package update

Writes pending-update.json under the Controller state directory for the privileged nex-controller-update path unit. Returns 202 scheduled; the helper runs apt-get update then apt-get install --only-upgrade nex-controller, so dependencies resolve and the package signature is verified, and restarts nex-controller. A failed upgrade restarts the service before reporting. Returns 503 when apply-update or the path unit is missing. Controller cannot run apt itself (ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges). Audits update.apply. Empty JSON body. CSRF and same-origin required.

POST /api/v1/vms/{id}/power

Request a VM power action on its assigned host

Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Requires an administrator session, same Origin and X-CSRF-Token. Persist request_id before sending; the same id replays the same durable operation, a different action under the same id is 409. The VM must be an adopted appliance or a successfully created guest; its assigned host must be freshly connected, unrevoked and report managed-vm-v1 and vm-power-v1, and queued power requires vm-power-queue-v1. With this capability, a pending power/edit/media request becomes a same-VM prerequisite instead of a busy refusal. Core persists FIFO admission order and executes after the prerequisite succeeds; failed, uncertain or missing prerequisites fail before effects. Without queue capability another pending task is 409. The request is audited as vm-power and delivered to the host in its next report; poll operations for the result. A succeeded shutdown or reboot means the ACPI request was issued, not that the guest honored it: the VM's observed state is the truth. Controller outage never stops a guest. Core-received commands survive agent restart and Controller replacement. Inventory.managed.outcomes exposes queued and terminal tasks for passive adoption without redispatch. Queue order concerns task completion, not guest ACPI completion; actual failures are not automatically retried.

POST /api/v1/hosts/{id}/console

Issue a single-use console ticket for a host

Requires an administrator session, same Origin and X-CSRF-Token, and an empty JSON object body. The host must be freshly connected, unrevoked and report capability host-console-v1 (distinct from console-v1, which only ever covers VM consoles; an agent without host-console-v1 gets 409 rather than a ticket it can never fulfil). The ticket is bound to the requesting session user and host, lives 60 seconds in Controller memory only, is delivered once to the host in its next report response with an empty vm_id (host console), and is consumed by the first matching WebSocket. Audited as host.console.open.

POST /api/v1/vms/{id}/media

Insert or eject ISO media on a VM CDROM

Queues a durable vm-media command on the VM assigned host. Requires administrator session, CSRF, stable request_id, action insert|eject, and media_id for insert of a verified ISO on that host. Host must report vm-media-v1. Both actions apply to a running VM, on pool-shared storage too: the record changes media_id only, so no boot order changes and no stop is required. Audited; operation appears in the operations list. Optional drive selects install (default) or drivers; drivers requires vm-media-drivers-drive-v1.

PUT /api/v1/vms/{id}

Replace a VM's definition on its assigned host

Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Requires an administrator session, same Origin and X-CSRF-Token. Persist request_id before sending; the same id replays the same durable operation, a different body under the same id is 409. The body is the complete desired definition (the same shape as creation); Controller validates its shape and references like creation, refuses immutable changes (an existing disk's storage, size or provisioning), and, when the VM is observed running, changes that need it stopped (name, CPU, memory, firmware, machine type, any boot order, an existing disk's bus, an existing interface's network, model, MAC or MTU, or adding a SATA disk); interfaces are matched by effective MAC: when the request names any current interface by its effective MAC (as the VM list reports it, and as the bundled editor sends every existing interface), every interface with an empty MAC is new; when it names none, an empty MAC is matched by position and the request is refused with 400 if it removes, reorders or changes an interface at an existing index, while an unchanged interface keeps the current address at its position. Clients that send any existing interface's MAC must send all of them, or an omitted one is replaced by a new interface. Controller freezes every automatic MAC into the definition before its stop-first check, drawing new ones from the VM's derived range at the first index above the highest one the current definition uses that no requested or current interface holds, or the lowest free index when none above is free, so a new interface never takes the address of one removed in the same edit, nor, unless the highest-index interface was removed or index 255 is in use, of one removed in an earlier edit; then it queues a vm-update command at revision current + 1 for the host's next report. Name and MAC uniqueness against other VMs and dedicated-memory admission are checked by the host against its journal and libvirt, as for creation. Core applies live what a running guest can take (adding or removing VirtIO/SCSI disks and interfaces, inserting, swapping or ejecting the ISO, description, guest OS hint and autostart) and redefines a shut-off guest from the regenerated XML; removed disks are detached and their files retained, never deleted. While validating a running guest's edit, before allocating any disk or changing any device, Core compares the live and persistent domains and reports the vm-update operation failed, changing nothing, with "network interface MAC <mac> is still attached to the running VM; wait for the guest to release it or stop the VM, then save again" when an added interface's MAC is still on a live interface that the guest has not released, changing nothing. The host reports the new definition as current and Controller refreshes its mirror from that report; poll operations for the result. One vm-update, vm-power or vm-media request per VM may be in flight. Nonempty cpu.features requires vm-cpu-baseline-v1 after idempotent replay (409 on older Core). Core validates the explicit named CPU definition with native hypervisor-cpu-compare against the actual machine before creation/stopped edits/Core-mediated starts. Existing model-only definitions retain prior semantics; no guest-OS-specific CPU filtering. Nonempty tags require vm-tags-v1 on the VM's host and its pool master after idempotent replay (409 on older Core); an edit that omits tags clears them.

DELETE /api/v1/vms/{id}

Delete a stopped guest VM on its assigned host

Implemented in development product 0.2.6, protocol v1. Requires an administrator session, same Origin and X-CSRF-Token. Persist request_id before sending; the same id replays the same durable operation, a different body under the same id is 409. Body delete_disks=false retains guest disk files on storage after undefine; delete_disks=true unlinks them after undefine. Requires observed shut off with fresh host report, vm-delete-v1 on the host, and refuses the Controller appliance. One vm-update, vm-power, vm-media or vm-delete request per VM may be in flight. Core journals the delete, reports a DeletedVMs tombstone, and Controller drops its vm-create mirror. Poll operations for the result; HTTP 202 is not proof the domain is gone. A new delete for a VM whose earlier delete was interrupted finishes that earlier delete when both requests make the same delete_disks choice, then fails with 'VM is already deleted on this host: an earlier interrupted delete has now finished' (or 'an earlier interrupted delete for this VM is still unresolved: <reason>'); with a different delete_disks choice Core refuses the new request without finishing the earlier one, so disks a later request asked to keep are never wiped.

POST /api/v1/media/download

Download a public ISO URL on Nex Core

Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. JSON rejects unknown fields and bodies over 1 MiB. Supply a stable request_id, verified storage_id, .iso basename name and public HTTP(S) url (at most 4096 characters; no userinfo or fragment). Controller queues iso-import on the selected storage host; it never fetches or stages URL bytes. New requests require a fresh active host with managed-vm-v1 and iso-download-v1. Identical retries return the original operation even while the host is unavailable; changed payload returns 409. Core validates public destinations on every DNS lookup and redirect without Controller credentials or environment proxies, bounds streaming to destination free space with a reserve, verifies ISO9660 and computes size/SHA-256 before publishing. Initial size_bytes=0 and sha256 empty; successful host inventory supplies verified metadata. URL is omitted from client responses and inventory. Poll media and operations for completion. Host journal owns download recovery; ambiguous interrupted imports require attention. Older hosts do not receive URL commands; uploading a local file remains available.

DELETE /api/v1/media/{id}

Discard a failed ISO import, or remove an imported ISO

Implemented in development product 0.2.8, protocol v1; the succeeded-import branch added in 0.3.5. Requires an administrator session, same Origin and X-CSRF-Token. For an iso-import whose operation is failed or needs_attention the call takes NO body and removes only this Controller's library record and its own staging bytes, so a download that failed does not occupy the library forever with no way to clear it (BUG-0203); no Core command is issued, no host state is touched, and the discard is audited as media.discard. For a SUCCEEDED import the call now relays a media-remove command to the host that stores the ISO (the pool master for pool-shared media) and requires a body {request_id}; no pool_id, host_id or expected_generation is accepted, because the pool, owner and current generation all come from the host-reported record. Core unlinks the published file, refuses while any VM on any host in the pool has the ISO in a CD drive (running or stopped) and while member VM inventory is stale, and journals a durable tombstone that members converge to; the library row disappears only when the host reports that tombstone. Retrying a failed download is POST /api/v1/media/download again under a NEW request_id; there is no separate retry operation. 409 when the import is still queued or dispatched, 409 while another media transfer holds the staging lock, and 409 when the owning host does not advertise pool-resource-removal-v1 (checked before the body is read, so an older client's bodyless call still gets the upgrade answer). 404 for an unknown id.

GET /api/v1/vms/{id}/stats

Read a VM's usage history

Administrator session; read-only and safe to retry. Relays the query to the VM’s assigned host over a stats channel the host dials out (first query waits up to one report heartbeat, then the channel is reused and closes after 5 minutes idle). The history is recorded and kept by Nex Core; the Controller stores nothing. Requires the host to be fresh, not revoked and to report usage-history-v1.

Read a host's usage history

Administrator session; read-only and safe to retry. POST /api/v1/agent/stats/{token}

Attach the host's outbound stats channel

Core sends this over its enrolled mTLS connection with Connection: Upgrade and Upgrade: nex-stats after receiving stats_channels in a report response. The token must name a pending channel for this exact host. After 101 the Controller writes HTTP/1.1 GET /stats?object=vm&id=<uuid>&range=<range> or GET /stats?object=host&range=<range> requests on the connection and Core answers each in order with a StatsHistory (200) or {"error"} (400 invalid query, 404 no history). Either side closes the connection on idle, restart or protocol error. Core never listens for inbound stats connections.

After 101 the Controller writes HTTP/1.1 GET /stats?object=vm&id=<uuid>&range=<range> or GET /stats?object=host&range=<range> requests on the connection and Core answers each in order with a StatsHistory (200) or {\"error\"} (400 invalid query, 404 no history). Either side closes the connection on idle, restart or protocol error. Core never listens for inbound stats connections.",

POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/master

Change the pool master of a pool

Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. Hands the pool authority from the current pool master to a ready member of the same pool, keeping the pool, its networks, its storage registrations, its ISO library and its virtual machines with their identities and their names. While the change runs the pool master refuses every pool authority write — placements, definitions, start admission, joins, maintenance and pool resource registrations — with a message asking the operator to retry; nothing is queued behind it. Running guests are unaffected, stop and force-stop are never refused, and storage reservation releases are deliberately never frozen. This route has no automatic action: it is an operator request against a cooperating master. Core separately supports automatic promotion in eligible two-host pools using a recorded usable BMC fence profile with Host fencing enabled. The Controller relays exactly one durable pool-transfer command to the pool's current master and stores nothing else: no stage, no timer, no generation, no membership. Core runs the whole transfer by itself, so a Controller restarted, replaced or disconnected mid-transfer changes nothing and re-projects the transfer from the hosts' next reports. The refusals below are only what the Controller can already see from host reports; Core checks every one of them again against its own record, and its own refusals arrive as a failed operation with conflict marked in last_transfer of GET /api/v1/pools/{id}/members, not as an HTTP status here. Implemented in development product 0.1.0.

POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/master/cancel

Cancel a master change or eject that has not handed the authority over

Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. Relays one pool-transfer command with action transfer-cancel to the current pool master. Core decides whether it is still possible: before the hand-off it clears the freeze and the current master stays master; after the hand-off it is allowed only when the target proves, under its own lock, that it never activated and never will for that operation, and otherwise refuses with "the target has already activated this pool authority; the master change can only go forward". Nothing is ever cancelled by a timeout. A cancel is not refused for a transfer already being in progress — that is what it cancels — and it gates on no host but the master. The Controller relays exactly one durable pool-transfer command to the pool's current master and stores nothing else: no stage, no timer, no generation, no membership. Core runs the whole transfer by itself, so a Controller restarted, replaced or disconnected mid-transfer changes nothing and re-projects the transfer from the hosts' next reports. The refusals below are only what the Controller can already see from host reports; Core checks every one of them again against its own record, and its own refusals arrive as a failed operation with conflict marked in last_transfer of GET /api/v1/pools/{id}/members, not as an HTTP status here. Implemented in development product 0.1.0.

DELETE /api/v1/pools/{id}/members/{host_id}

Eject a member from a pool

Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. Removes a member from the pool; the ejected host re-initializes itself as the pool master of a new single-host pool named after its hostname, keeping its host ID, its enrollment, its local storage and its local virtual machines, and the Controller adopts that new pool from the host's own report under the same site. Its certificate stops being an admitted pool peer, and the pool's shared networks, storage registrations and ISO library are no longer available to it. Core refuses the eject while the host still owns any pool VM record or still holds a pool-shared storage reservation; those two refusals are deliberately not pre-checked here, because they are Core's decision, and they arrive on the operation. A member that is not reporting can be ejected: neither its freshness nor its capability list is gated, and it learns of the eject when it returns. The pool master cannot be ejected; change the pool master first. The Controller relays exactly one durable pool-transfer command to the pool's current master and stores nothing else: no stage, no timer, no generation, no membership. Core runs the whole transfer by itself, so a Controller restarted, replaced or disconnected mid-transfer changes nothing and re-projects the transfer from the hosts' next reports. The refusals below are only what the Controller can already see from host reports; Core checks every one of them again against its own record, and its own refusals arrive as a failed operation with conflict marked in last_transfer of GET /api/v1/pools/{id}/members, not as an HTTP status here. Implemented in development product 0.1.0.

POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/master/promote/preflight

Ask a surviving member what blocks its promotion

Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. One brokered report round trip to the named promotion candidate (pool request action promotion-preflight): the candidate computes the whole verdict on Core from its own signed authority replica and its own live probes of the pool network, and the Controller mirrors the answer verbatim. Nothing is stored, journalled or audited and no command is issued, so this is safe to call repeatedly. The pool master is deliberately not required to be fresh, and its reachability from this Controller is never evidence in either direction: a preflight is exactly what an operator runs when the master is gone, and Core alone probes it. old-master-exclusion is normally unknown here, because Core fences and proves it during the promotion and never during a preflight; ready_to_fence, not can_promote, is the flag that says confirming now proceeds to the fence rather than to a refusal. Implemented in development product 0.1.0.

POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/master/promote

Promote a surviving member after Nex Core fences the old pool master

Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. The operator action for a pool master that is gone. Exactly one durable pool-promote command is journaled, addressed to the candidate — the one pool command besides pool-join that does not go to the master, because the master is the host that is gone. confirmation is the pool's name, typed; fence_confirmed must be literally true and is the operator's separate acknowledgement that the old pool master will be powered off. Neither is evidence: Core produces and verifies the fence proof itself, no proof crosses the wire, and the acknowledgement is a precondition only. There is no expected_version, because the generation to check against is the dead master's and the candidate re-proves the whole verdict immediately before it activates. Nothing about the old master is pre-refused here — whether it answers, whether this Controller can reach it, when it was last seen — and neither is a missing or unusable fence profile, a lagging replica, a VM ownership conflict or a member holding a higher authority: all of those are Core's decision at run time and arrive asynchronously on the operation, surfaced verbatim in last_promotion. The Controller stores no verdict, fence proof, restriction, stage, candidate or generation, so a Controller restarted or replaced mid-promotion knows nothing about it until the hosts report and then re-projects it. This route remains an explicit manual promotion. Separately, Core supports a narrow automatic promotion for eligible two-host pools using a recorded BMC fence profile; it requires Host fencing enabled and does not use watchdog, storage lease or Nex Witness. The automatic path is owned and resumed by Core, not triggered by this route. No force, override, "declare host lost" or timeout-based path exists or may be added. Implemented in development product 0.1.0.

POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/members/{host_id}/fence-profile

Record or clear how a member of this pool would be power-fenced

Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. The profile is a field of the durable membership record the pool master owns, so this is the one promotion route relayed to the master and the one that needs a fresh one. One durable pool-fence-profile command is journaled; a null fence clears the profile. An optional credential is never stored by this Controller: it is handed to Core over the existing one-time encrypted credential handoff, Core allocates its own private reference, and only that opaque reference is written into the command — nothing reaches SQLite, the audit trail, the response or any log, and the stored replay payload is the profile as sent, so an exact retry stays byte-identical. Core then refuses asynchronously to record a profile whose material it does not hold, and refuses at record time any profile it could not verify. Recording a redfish profile is a live operation on Core: it connects to the controller, pins the certificate it presents, and proves the machine before the profile enters the membership, so an unreachable or wrong controller is refused now rather than during a promotion. Before any power-off Nex Core asks the management controller which machine it manages — IPMI Get System GUID, in either documented byte order, or the Redfish ComputerSystem.UUID — and compares it with the target host's own SMBIOS system UUID in the master's membership record. A mismatch, a missing recorded UUID and an unreadable controller each refuse the fence and power nothing off. A management controller is therefore recordable for a host that has reported its system UUID, which is how a physical pool is fenced; the virsh profile remains for a Nex Core running as a virtual machine in a disposable lab. Recording a usable profile for the pool master itself is what opts a pool into fence-verified promotion, and with it into the restart rule a restricted master follows. Implemented in development product 0.1.0.

POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/members/{host_id}/bmc-probe

Detect how a member's management controller answers

Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. One brokered report round trip to the pool master (pool request action bmc-probe), which probes the address itself — HTTPS Redfish and IPMI RMCP+ — from the host that would fence, and recommends a kind and system Id or plug. It takes the fence profile's gates: a fresh pool master with pool-authority-transfer-v1 whose reported membership includes the host. An optional password uses the one-time handoff with a probe-only bmc_probe purpose. Core removes both private credential copies after execution and expires an undelivered handoff after 10 minutes on its local probe tick or next startup. No discovery result or pool setting is stored, journalled or audited and no command is issued, so Detect is safe to repeat with a new request_id; recording the result is Set BMC access (POST .../fence-profile), which proves the controller again. The relay waits up to 3 minutes, because Core gives a probe up to 2 minutes and answers on its next report.

      "description": "Refused without asking anything: \"the pool master must be fresh and active to record a fence profile\", \"recording a fence profile needs pool-authority-transfer-v1 on the pool master; upgrade <host>\", \"the pool master has not reported its membership; a fence profile cannot be recorded yet\", \"no such member of this pool\", \"request_id already used with another credential payload\", \"pool request is already active\".",
      "content": {
        "application/json": {
          "schema": {
            "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "499": {
      "description": "The client disconnected before the master answered (\"the client disconnected before the pool master finished probing the management controller; detect again\"). The broker entry is released.",
      "content": {
        "application/json": {
          "schema": {
            "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "500": {
      "description": "Controller storage failure (\"storage unavailable\", \"inventory unavailable\"). Nothing was asked; safe to retry.",
      "content": {
        "application/json": {
          "schema": {
            "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "503": {
      "description": "\"Core did not acknowledge fence credential delivery; retry with the same request_id\". Nothing was probed.",
      "content": {

          "schema": {
            "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "504": {
      "description": "The master did not answer within 3 minutes (\"the pool master did not finish probing the management controller before the deadline; detect again\"). The body is a PoolResult with status failed. Nothing was written.",
      "content": {

            "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolResult"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

DELETE /api/v1/storage/{id}

Discard a storage registration the pool master refused

Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. The storage twin of the failed ISO import's discard. A registration a host refused published nothing anywhere: it is this Controller's own request history, not pool state, so discarding it deletes only the Controller's managed_resources row, relays nothing to any host, takes no body and keeps the operation and its audit history. It audits storage.discard. The guard is narrow on purpose: a row whose command a host has since reported as applied is refused, so this can never delete the projection of a live repository. A repository a host does hold is removed by relaying a detach, never by this route. Implemented in development product 0.3.5.

GET /api/v1/hosts/{id}/hardware

Read a host's hardware

Administrator session; read-only and safe to retry. Relays one live observation to the host over the same stats channel the host dials out, as GET /hardware. The host reads its system, CPU, memory modules, disks, PCI devices and temperature sensors on request and stores none of it; the Controller stores none of it either, so a replacement Controller sees the same report. A section whose source is missing or fails is returned unavailable with a reason and the rest of the report still returns. Serial numbers are returned to authenticated administrators only and are never logged. Requires the host to be fresh, not revoked and to report host-hardware-v1.

POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/members/{host_id}/bmc-provisioning

Let a host configure its own management controller for fencing again

Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. Whether a host may configure its own management controller is a field of the durable membership record the pool master owns, so this is relayed to the master and takes the same membership and capability check a fence profile does. One durable pool-bmc-provisioning command is journaled for the master, which clears the host's bmc_provisioning_disabled flag and drops its last management-controller report; the host reads the decision from the pool records it already holds and creates the account on its next reconcile pass, because reporting a fence device before it exists would claim one that is not there. It is a desired state, not a transition: a host that is already allowed answers succeeded. There is no request to turn it off — clearing the host's fence device through POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/members/{host_id}/fence-profile with a null fence is what withdraws a Core-provisioned device, removes the account from the controller and stops this host configuring it again, so one operator action has one meaning. Nex Controller stores nothing of its own: the decision lives in the master's membership and a fresh Controller recovers it from the master's reported inventory. Implemented in development product 0.4.2.

POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/host-fencing

Turn this pool's host fencing on or off

Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. Host fencing is one pool-wide setting in the durable membership record the pool master owns, so this is relayed to the master and takes the same freshness check a fence profile does, plus pool-host-fencing-v1 on the master. One durable pool-host-fencing command is journaled for the master, which records the setting and replicates it with the pool's records; every host reads it from the copy it already holds. It is a desired state, not a transition: re-sending the state the master already records answers succeeded. Turning it on arms nothing by itself — Nex Core arms a host's watchdog only where every prerequisite the master reports in PoolFenceSummary.prerequisites holds, and until this pool runs a quorum service the quorum line is unknown and nothing is armed. It is on for a pool that has never been told otherwise. Nex Controller stores nothing of its own: the setting lives in the master's membership and a fresh Controller recovers it from the master's reported inventory. Implemented in development product 0.4.2.

POST /api/v1/hosts/{id}/system-disk

Replace a failed disk of a host's system mirror

Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. Relays one durable host-system-disk-replace command to the host, which revalidates the array and the disk against its own observation and then clears the replacement, copies the partition table from the surviving member's disk with sgdisk --replicate and randomises its identifiers, adds the new member with mdadm --add, and makes the disk bootable the way the installer does for that firmware: on BIOS grub-install --target=i386-pc on the disk itself (firmware branch on /sys/firmware/efi; the installer still places an ESP on every mirror member, but that path does not format it), and on UEFI mkfs.vfat on the replacement's copy of the surviving disk's ESP followed by the host's own nex-sync-esp copier, or the same copy of /boot/efi/EFI including the removable fallback path when that helper is absent or copied nothing. The kernel rebuilds the mirror afterwards; the host and its VMs keep running and nothing waits on the Controller. The Controller computes nothing and stores nothing but the task: the mirror's state comes from the host hardware report. The refusals below are only what the Controller can already see from this host's reports; Core checks the array, the disk, its size and the erase confirmation again, and its own refusals arrive as a failed operation rather than as an HTTP status here. Implemented in development product 0.4.4.

      "description": "The host is revoked, it is not freshly connected (\"the host must be freshly connected before its system disk is replaced\"), its Nex Core is too old (\"replacing a system disk needs host-system-disk-replace-v1 on this host; upgrade Nex Core\"), or the request_id was already used with another payload.",
      "content": {
        "application/json": {
          "schema": {
            "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "500": {
      "description": "Controller storage failure.",
      "content": {
        "application/json": {
          "schema": {
            "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Error"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

POST /api/v1/vms/{id}/backup

Back up a VM now

Omitted or stopped requires a shut-off guest. crash is online crash-consistent push-mode backup. quiesced is refused until proven. UEFI online capture is refused in this development slice. Exact retry reuses the retained operation; changed input returns 409. Controller queues on the pool master with the VM owner host; the master dispatches member work over the authenticated Core peer route. Core owns publication.

UEFI online capture is refused in this development slice. Exact retry reuses the retained operation; changed input returns 409. Controller queues on the pool master with the VM owner host; the master dispatches member work over the authenticated Core peer route. Core owns publication.",

POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/backup-test-verify

Record test restore result

Records the operator's passed/failed observation only after Core proves the current VM belongs to the exact successful test restore. Passed requires intact current disks and firmware; failed permits damaged artifacts if the native creator and definition still match. A member-owned VM is checked through authenticated Core peer origin proof. Missing or changed provenance is refused; uncertain transport retains a retryable Core metadata receipt.

Schemas and authentication

securitySchemes

AdminSession
{
  "type": "apiKey",
  "in": "cookie",
  "name": "__Host-nex_session",
  "description": "Administrator session cookie __Host-nex_session, Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict, Path=/ with no Domain. Expires after 30 minutes without an authenticated mutation or eight hours absolutely. GET/HEAD polling does not extend idle lifetime; mutations also require matching Origin and X-CSRF-Token. At most 64 active sessions per service. Legacy unprefixed cookies are refused; sign in again after upgrading.",
  "x-session-policy": {
    "idle_timeout_seconds": 1800,
    "absolute_timeout_seconds": 28800,
    "maximum_sessions": 64,
    "idle_refresh": "authenticated mutations after Origin/CSRF validation; GET and HEAD never extend it",
    "legacy_cookies_accepted": false
  }
}
HostCertificate
{
  "type": "mutualTLS",
  "description": "Unique signed host certificate; current enrollment and revocation are checked on each request."
}

schemas

Site
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "name": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "id",
    "name"
  ],
  "x-go-type": "protocol.Site",
  "example": {
    "id": "<site-id>",
    "name": "Home"
  }
}
Pool
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "site_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "name": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "master_host_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Host that controls this pool. Empty only for databases migrated from the removed manual pool creation with no host."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "id",
    "site_id",
    "name",
    "master_host_id"
  ],
  "x-go-type": "protocol.Pool",
  "example": {
    "id": "<pool-id>",
    "site_id": "<site-id>",
    "name": "core-01",
    "master_host_id": "<host-id>"
  }
}
Check
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Nonblank after trimming; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR/LF/NUL."
    },
    "status": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "healthy",
        "degraded",
        "failed",
        "unknown",
        "unsupported"
      ]
    },
    "observed_at": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date-time"
    },
    "last_success": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "string",
          "format": "date-time"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ]
    },

On each managed report Controller adopts, under actor system, every entry it does not hold (request_id adopt-<kind>:<host>:<id>, kind storage-register | network-register | iso-import | vm-create), reusing the resource ID and recording the operation as already succeeded without dispatching a command; it also rebuilds its appliances record from appliances and records outcomes as operations. Entries that duplicate an existing ID, storage path, network (kind, source) or VM name, invalid entries, entries whose references are not adopted on the host and VMs listed in missing_vms are not adopted; each leaves one needs_attention operation and an audit entry (see ManagedState). ReportRequest
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "version": {
      "type": "integer",
      "enum": [
        1,
        2
      ],
      "description": "Version 1 is the legacy managed-VM report. A Core starts storage negotiation with version 2 but without storage-repositories-v1, waits for storage_repositories acknowledgement, persists it, then advertises the capability."
    },
    "sequence": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1,
      "maximum": 9223372036854775807
    },
    "inventory": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Inventory"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Omit or null for heartbeat only; prior inventory remains unchanged and is not made healthy."
    },
    "results": {
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Result"
      },
      "maxItems": 100
    },
    "capabilities": {
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "type": "string",
        "x-max-utf8-bytes": 100
      },
      "maxItems": 32,
      "description": "Advertised on every report. managed-vm-v1 enables managed command delivery. pool-vm-placement-v1 means Core supports the fail-closed master-owned placement preflight for VM definition transitions. storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 offers the additive clustered session-monitor projection; it must be acknowledged through storage_clusters_support before Core sends that projection. Omission or null disables managed delivery for this report; a newer sequence also replaces stored capabilities. vm-cpu-baseline-v1 advertises generic fixed CPU feature support and native pool baseline discovery; upgrade Controller before Core for additive fields."
    },
    "storage_discoveries": {
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/components/schemas/StorageDiscoveryResult"
      },
      "description": "One-shot sanitized results from prior report-response discovery requests. Never journaled or adopted."
    },
    "storage_clusters": {
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/components/schemas/StorageClusterResult"
      },
      "description": "Transient results for addressed clustered-storage requests, emitted only after the exact v2 storage_clusters_support acknowledgement. session_monitor_ready and monitor-stage members are included only after the offered storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 extension is acknowledged. The result exposes Core-owned durable operation state but is not Controller state."
    },
    "pool_results": {
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolResult"
      },
      "maxItems": 32,
      "description": "Answers to the pool_requests this host received on an earlier report response, sent by a Core advertising pool-join-v1. More than 32 results is a malformed report (400). The Controller matches each result to its one pending in-memory request and keeps nothing afterwards."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "version",
    "sequence"
  ],
  "x-go-type": "protocol.ReportRequest",
  "example": {
    "version": 2,
    "sequence": 1,
    "results": []
  },
  "description": "Version and sequence are required by runtime validation. Results may be omitted or null and defaults to no results. Inventory may be omitted or null for heartbeat only. Clustered results and storage-clustered-iscsi-v2 are withheld until this Controller connection acknowledges storage_clusters_support. The additive session-monitor members are withheld unless the Core offered and the Controller acknowledged storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1. Both acknowledgements reset after a cluster preflight failure, reconnect or Controller re-enrolment. Version-one reports retain existing non-storage behavior.",
  "x-go-emitted-fields": [
    "version",
    "sequence",
    "results"
  ]

StorageClusterFence
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "kind": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "redfish",
        "ipmilan",
        "virsh",
        "scsi_pr"
      ]
    },
    "endpoint": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "target_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "username": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Management-controller account for redfish and ipmilan, with power control only. It is not a secret and is reported back; its password is the credential. Absent on virsh and scsi_pr profiles, and a BMC profile without one can never produce a proof."
    },
    "tls_fingerprint": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$",
      "description": "Core captures the certificate the controller presents when the profile is recorded, keeps its leaf SHA-256 here and holds every later connection to exactly it: a factory management controller is self-signed with no usable name, so this pin, not a chain, identifies the endpoint the password is sent to and the power-off is issued through. A changed certificate refuses the fence with its own sentence rather than as a network fault. Reported so an operator can compare it with the controller's own page; it is not a secret and a client never supplies one. Absent on ipmilan, which authenticates its RMCP+ session and presents no certificate, and on virsh and scsi_pr."
    },
    "credential_ref": {
      "type": "string",
      "writeOnly": true
    },
    "device_path": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "virsh_uri": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "For virsh, exactly qemu:///system or qemu+ssh://<ssh_login>@<endpoint>[:<ssh_port>]/system. The latter must match the pinned SSH fields; it rejects passwords, query strings, fragments and every other URI path. An omitted URI port is valid only when ssh_port is 22."
    },
    "ssh_login": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "ssh_port": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0
    },
    "ssh_host_key_ref": {
      "type": "string",
      "writeOnly": true
    },
    "cipher": {
      "type": "integer",
      "enum": [
        3,
        17
      ],
      "description": "The RMCP+ cipher suite an ipmilan fence must use, as the controller's own LAN channel offers it. Core selects it itself \u2014 17 where the controller offers it, otherwise 3, the suite every IPMI 2.0 controller must implement \u2014 either while provisioning the account in-band or while proving a profile an operator entered. Suite 0 asks for no authentication, no integrity and no confidentiality, so it is never selected and never accepted here. Absent means none was recorded and ipmitool's own default is used. A client never supplies it; a request that does is refused with 400."
    },
    "provisioned_by_core": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "The account behind this profile is one Nex Core created on the host's own management controller in-band. It is how a host knows, after a reboot or a master change, that the account under the Nex name is its own to replace rather than somebody else's to leave alone, and it is why an operator-entered profile is never overwritten by automatic provisioning. Written only by the pool master when the host's own Core reports the account it created; a client never supplies it, and a request that does is refused with 400."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "kind"
  ],
  "x-go-type": "protocol.StorageClusterFence",
  "description": "Closed Core fence profile. credential_ref and ssh_host_key_ref are opaque names for root-only Core secrets, never secret bytes; arbitrary commands and arguments are not accepted. Before any power-off Core asks the management controller which machine it manages \u2014 the Redfish ComputerSystem.UUID, compared exactly, or IPMI Get System GUID, where either documented byte order counts \u2014 and compares it with the target host's own SMBIOS system UUID in the master's membership record. A mismatch, a host with no unique hardware identity and an unreadable controller each refuse the fence and power nothing off. Redirects are never followed, so the identity cannot be read from one machine while another is powered off. A Redfish fence is performed by Core itself over the pinned connection \u2014 identity GET, ComputerSystem.Reset ForceOff, then a separate PowerState read \u2014 rather than by fence_redfish, which cannot be bound to the recorded certificate. virsh is for a Nex Core running as a virtual machine in a disposable lab and remains unaccepted for native production use."
}

ZFSReplaceRequest
{
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Replace one failed leaf device of a provisioned ZFS repository's pool on one host. old_device names the leaf exactly as the pool observation reports it, and device is one candidate from POST /api/v1/storage/discover with kind zfs-device, carrying the same identity, fingerprint and typed erase confirmation rules the ZFS wizard uses. Core revalidates both against a fresh observation of the pool and the disk before it touches anything.",
  "properties": {
    "operation_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Core operation identity. The executing host journals its replacement under it, so a redelivered command replays the recorded outcome instead of acting again."
    },

      "type": "string"
    },
    "pool_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "host_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The configured host whose pool holds the failed disk. It may be the pool master or a ready current member."
    },
    "old_device": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The failed leaf's /dev/disk/by-id path, as the repository's pool observation reports it."

}

PoolMember
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "host_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "certificate_sha256": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "generation": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0
    },
    "status": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "observed_at": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date-time",
      "description": "When the master admitted this member, or created the pool for its founding host. Nothing rewrites it afterwards; the Controller reports it as joined_at."
    },
    "error": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "peer_origin": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Bare HTTPS origin this member advertised to the master for peer traffic. Recorded from the member's own advertisement, or, for the master's own row, from the master_url of the first Controller-driven join, which the master works out itself when none is supplied; never inferred from Controller connectivity."
    },
    "system_uuid": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "This host's own SMBIOS system UUID, 32 lower-case hex digits without separators, reported by the host itself while it was alive: at join, and on every reconcile pass, so a pool formed before this existed gains it without re-joining. It is what proves a management controller belongs to this machine before it is powered off. Like peer_origin it is a recorded observation and moves no generation. A host too old to report one stays empty and simply cannot be given a BMC fence device."
    },
    "maintenance": {
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "maintenance_since": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date-time"
    },
    "replica_ack_excluded": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Core-owned exclusion from snapshot reservation/settlement replica acknowledgements and ordinary replica-push failure aggregation, recorded only by a supported promotion after validating fresh exact fence evidence. Omitted means false. The host remains a pool member and VM owner; delivery is still attempted. The master clears the exclusion only after accepted current-membership VM inventory and an exact current-generation/content replica POST acknowledgement. Covered by the signed authority content, without changing membership generation when cleared. It does not exempt destructive resource-removal acknowledgements, storage-lease preparation, restart authority confirmation or future promotion fencing. Use matching development Core builds; old promotions are not retroactively excluded."
    },
    "replica_generation": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "The master's observation of the authority-replica generation this member last acknowledged. Memory-only on the master and overlaid on the reported copy of the membership record: it is never written into the durable membership and is never an input to the generation equality rule. A member that has never acknowledged one is reported at 0, honestly."
    },
    "replica_digest": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Content digest the member acknowledged, as observed by the master."
    },
    "replica_error": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 200,
      "description": "The master's bounded reason for the last failed push to this member: \"pool member does not support pool-authority-replica-v2; upgrade it before relying on its replica\", \"pool member did not report its authority replica\", \"pool member did not acknowledge the authority replica\", \"pool member acknowledged the replica without joining the authority sanlock lockspace\", \"pool member refused the authority replica\" or the member's own refusal text, \"pool authority replica exceeds the peer body limit\", or \"pool member peer certificate cannot receive a wrapped pool CA key\", \"pool member reported invalid backup authority page progress\", or a refusal to report/stage a signed backup authority page."
    },
    "replica_observed_at": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date-time",
      "description": "When the master made that observation. Zero when it has none."
    },
    "fence": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/StorageClusterFence"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "How this host would be excluded from the pool if it had to be fenced: the same closed typed profile clustered storage already uses, recorded in the master's durable membership and replicated with it, so a promoted master inherits it and a fresh Controller re-adopts it. Only a virsh profile can be recorded by this build; Core refuses to record a profile it cannot verify. The credential reference it carries is never projected to a client, and neither is anything the reference names."
    },
    "fence_credential_version": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "The master's counter for the private fence credential material behind this host's profile. The material itself is never in the membership; only this number is, so rotating it changes the replicated content and therefore advances the pool authority generation, while re-recording identical material moves nothing."
    },
    "fence_readiness": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolFenceReadiness"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The pool master's own answer to whether this host could be shut out, per method. Reported only by the master, only for the membership it owns, and never written into the durable record. Absent from a Core too old to report it, which a Controller shows as \"not reported\" and never as ready."
    },
    "system_uuid_conflict_host_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The member that already reported the hardware identity this host reports, when the master refused this host's report because of it. Without it the refusal is a dead end: an operator is told their host has no unique identity with nothing to act on. Cleared the moment the identity is accepted."
    },
    "bmc": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolHostBMC"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "What this host's own Core found and did about its own management controller, reported to the master over the existing advertise peer route. It is an observation and a result, never a credential."
    },
    "bmc_provisioning_disabled": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "The operator's own decision, recorded by the master, that this host must not configure its management controller for fencing. Clearing a fence device Nex Core provisioned sets it \u2014 one operator action with one meaning \u2014 and the host removes the account it created when it sees it. It is a decision, not an observation, so it lives with the fence profile in the replicated membership and a host cannot set or clear it by reporting about itself."
    },
    "watchdog": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolHostWatchdog"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "This host's own watchdog capability, reported by the host and recorded by the master. A member too old to report one leaves it null, which is never counted."
    },
    "watchdog_armed": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolWatchdogArmed"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "That host's own report that it has armed its watchdog, recorded durably by the master. Null means the host never said, which is never a watchdog exclusion proof."
    },
    "sanlock_host_id": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "Pool-master-assigned stable sanlock host ID. Zero or absent means this legacy member cannot participate in a storage lease."
    },
    "sanlock_host_generation": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "Last native sanlock generation this host itself observed while its configured lease ID was live; not a proof by itself."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "host_id",
    "certificate_sha256",
    "generation",
    "status",
    "observed_at",
    "maintenance_since",
    "replica_observed_at"
  ],
  "x-go-type": "protocol.PoolMember"
}
