{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "pool_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "master_host_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "generation": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0
    },
    "members": {
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolMember"
      }
    },
    "host_fencing_disabled": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "The pool's Host fencing setting, recorded the way it is decided: fencing is on for a pool that has never been told otherwise, so an absent field is on and a record written before the setting existed keeps the default. It is a decision, so it is durable, replicated and only ever written by the master."
    },
    "fence_summary": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolFenceSummary"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The pool's fencing count, setting and prerequisite checklist, computed by the master over this membership when it reports it. Like the readiness on each member row it is a memory-only observation overlaid on the reported copy and never part of the durable record."
    },
    "witness": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolWitnessRecord"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The master's durable qdevice witness selection and CA pin. Runtime readiness is re-established from the native cluster after restart."
    },
    "next_sanlock_host_id": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "Monotonic host-ID allocator watermark; prevents reuse after a member is ejected."
    },
    "storage_lease": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolStorageLeaseConfig"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Reserved durable storage-lease configuration. The current product does not expose an accepted operator setup or automatic promotion workflow for it."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "pool_id",
    "master_host_id",
    "generation",
    "members"
  ],
  "x-go-type": "protocol.PoolMembership"
}
PoolCommand
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "request_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "action": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "membership": {
      "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolMembership",
      "description": "The full membership record for the pool actions that carry one. For join and maintenance only master_host_id is set: the master reads its own record, and a membership composed in the Controller could already be stale."
    },
    "member_endpoint": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "repository_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "expected_version": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "The membership generation the operator saw. 0 or absent means unchecked. For action maintenance it is compared against the master's own current membership generation, not against the membership on the wire."
    },
    "member_host_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 128,
      "description": "For action join, the joining host: it is the command's target, and the pool-join command is the one pool command not delivered to the master. For action maintenance it names the host being drained, which is not the target: that command goes to the master, addressed by membership.master_host_id."
    },
    "enabled": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "For action maintenance, the desired drain state of member_host_id. It is a desired state, not a transition: re-sending the state the host is already in succeeds and leaves maintenance_since unmoved."
    },
    "master_url": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 512,
      "description": "Bare HTTPS origin of the master's pool-peer listener that the joining Core dials. Required for action join."
    },
    "pool_ca_pem": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 16384,
      "writeOnly": true,
      "description": "Master's pool CA, pinned by the joining Core for the peer exchange. Required for action join. Never returned by any Controller read route."
    },
    "invitation": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 8192,
      "writeOnly": true,
      "description": "Single-use, 15-minute, pool- and host-bound join credential issued by the master and redeemed by the joining Core itself. Required for action join. The Controller relays it and never returns, lists, logs or audits it; the stored command row is scrubbed of this field and pool_ca_pem as soon as the operation leaves queued, and unconditionally 15 minutes after issue."
    },
    "peer_origin": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 512,
      "description": "Optional bare HTTPS origin the joining host advertises to its new master after it is admitted."
    },
    "fence": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/StorageClusterFence"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The power-fence profile to record for member_host_id, on action fence-profile. null clears the recorded profile. Any credential the operator supplied has already been delivered to Core over the one-time encrypted credential handoff before this command is written, and only the opaque reference Core allocated appears here."
    },
    "fence_confirmed": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "The operator's separate, explicit acknowledgement that promoting this candidate powers the old pool master off. It is a precondition and nothing else: Core produces and verifies the fence proof itself, no proof ever crosses this wire, and an acknowledgement is never evidence of anything."
    },
    "fence_host_ids": {
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "description": "The exact set of hosts the operator agreed to power off, as the verdict's fence_host_ids named them. Core compares it against the set it computes again at run time and refuses the promotion if they differ, so the fence can never widen between the confirmation and the act."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "request_id",
    "action",
    "membership"
  ],
  "x-go-type": "protocol.PoolCommand",
  "description": "membership is required for the member-join and storage-reconcile actions and is absent for join and maintenance: a joining host is not a member yet, and the master reads its own membership rather than trusting a Controller mirror. Valid() requires request_id plus, for action join, member_host_id, master_url, pool_ca_pem and invitation within the lengths above."
}
AddPoolMemberRequest
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "request_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 200,
      "description": "Stable client-generated idempotency key. Reuse it verbatim to retry; any changed field conflicts."
    },
    "host_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 200,
      "description": "The enrolled host to add. It must currently be the master of its own single-host pool."
    },
    "peer_origin": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 512,
      "description": "Bare https origin (scheme, host and port only, no path, query, fragment or userinfo) the joining host will advertise to its new master, for example https://192.0.2.12:9444. At most one trailing \"/\" is accepted and normalised away, exactly as the host-local join route accepts it; the normalised slash-less form is stored and forwarded, so the two spellings are the same request for exact-retry replay rather than a changed payload."
    },
    "master_url": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 512,
      "description": "Optional bare https origin of the master's pool-peer listener. Ignored when the master has already advertised its own peer origin. When omitted the master works out its own origin from its configured pool-peer listener (the listener's port, and its address when bound to one; the default-route source address for a wildcard bind), and refuses the join if it has no default route; masters built before this rule refuse an omitted master_url. At most one trailing \"/\" is accepted and normalised away, exactly as the host-local join route accepts it; the normalised slash-less form is stored and forwarded, so the two spellings are the same request for exact-retry replay rather than a changed payload."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "request_id",
    "host_id",
    "peer_origin"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
PoolJoinAccepted
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "host_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The joining host the command was addressed to."
    },
    "peer_origin": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "operation": {
      "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Operation"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "host_id",
    "peer_origin",
    "operation"
  ],
  "description": "Deliberately narrow: who was asked to join and the durable operation that asked. It never carries the invitation, the pool CA or the master URL."
}
PoolMembersView
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "pool_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "pool_name": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "master_host_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "master_connection": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "fresh",
        "stale",
        "unknown",
        "revoked"
      ]
    },
    "master_seen_at": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "When the pool master host last reported to this Controller, RFC3339, or \"\" when it has never reported. It is this Controller's own record of a host report, never a pool fact, projected from the hosts row it already keeps, so nothing new is stored for it. It is deliberately not gated on freshness: a stale-master banner needs exactly \"has not reported since <master_seen_at>\", and a fresh Controller that has never heard from the master says so rather than inventing a time."
    },
    "generation": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "Membership generation as reported by the master; 0 when the master has reported no membership."
    },
    "authoritative": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "True only while master_connection is fresh. When false, every observational master-reported field \u2014 status, error, checks, access counts, failures, maintenance and maintenance_since \u2014 is blank, null or unknown and must be presented as unknown rather than as the last known good state. peer_origin, the member's own reported join, its guests and the Controller's own last_maintenance are not master observations and are still reported."
    },
    "maintenance_supported": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "The pool master advertises pool-maintenance-v1. False means no maintenance control may be offered at all, because the refusal that makes the flag mean anything lives in the master."
    },
    "replica_supported": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "The pool master advertises pool-authority-replica-v2. False means no member can hold a replica and every member row reports state unsupported."
    },
    "transfer_supported": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "The pool master advertises pool-authority-transfer-v1. False means no master change and no eject is offered at all; the selected host's own capability is checked by the route."
    },
    "authority": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolAuthorityRecord"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The pool master's own reported authority record, mirrored verbatim. null when the master is not fresh or reports none. It is the only absolute generation in the pool; the Controller derives none."
    },
    "transfer": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolTransferStatus"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The pool master's own report of a transfer. null when the master is not fresh or reports none: a stale master's last transfer is never shown as present truth. Each participant's own view is on its member row."
    },
    "last_transfer": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolTransferOperation"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The newest pool-transfer command this Controller relayed for this pool, so an asynchronous Core refusal is visible where the operator acted. null when there is none."
    },
    "master_conflict": {
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "description": "Host IDs whose reported membership contradicts the recorded master without being evidence this Controller may adopt, which is exactly two cases: a host whose own membership names itself master at exactly the generation mirrored for the recorded master, and a host reporting a strictly higher generation for a master that is neither itself nor the recorded one. A strictly higher generation reported by the very host its membership names as master is the adoption rule's evidence and is followed rather than shown, and a fenced old master reporting at its old, strictly lower generation is not a rival claim at all. Normally empty; never acted on, only shown."
    },
    "promotion": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolPromotionView"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "A candidate's own reported fence-verified promotion, mirrored verbatim and stored nowhere. null when no fresh host of this pool reports one."
    },
    "last_promotion": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolTransferOperation"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The newest pool-promote command this Controller relayed for the pool, so an asynchronous Core refusal is visible where the operator acted. conflict marks refusals a synchronous route would have answered with 409; retryable is always false for a promotion, because nothing about one is retried unchanged \u2014 the blocking condition has to change first."
    },
    "members": {
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolMemberView"
      }
    },
    "host_fencing_supported": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "The pool master advertises pool-host-fencing-v1. Without it there is no Host fencing switch, because the setting that means anything is the master's."
    },
    "fence": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolFenceSummary"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The pool's own fencing answer as the master reported it with its membership. Mirrored verbatim and stored nowhere; null when the master is not fresh or is too old to report one, which reads as not reported and never as ready."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "pool_id",
    "pool_name",
    "master_host_id",
    "master_connection",
    "master_seen_at",
    "generation",
    "authoritative",
    "maintenance_supported",
    "replica_supported",
    "transfer_supported",
    "authority",
    "transfer",
    "last_transfer",
    "master_conflict",
    "promotion",
    "last_promotion",
    "members",
    "host_fencing_supported",
    "fence"
  ]
}
PoolMemberView
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "host_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Host name from the Controller's host record; empty for a reported member this Controller does not know."
    },
    "role": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "master",
        "member"
      ]
    },
    "status": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "ready",
        "pending",
        "failed",
        "ejected",
        "unknown"
      ],
      "description": "The master's own membership status for this host. unknown when the master is not fresh, and for the synthesised single row shown when the master has reported no membership at all."
    },
    "error": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "peer_origin": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Part of the master's durable membership record, not an observation of it: it is how this member is reached, and a quiet master does not make it untrue, so it is reported whether or not authoritative is true. Empty when the master has recorded none."
    },
    "joined_at": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "RFC 3339 UTC time the pool master admitted this member, or created the pool for its founding host: the observed_at of the master's durable membership record, which nothing rewrites after admission. Like peer_origin it is a record, reported whether or not authoritative is true. Empty when the reported record has none. Introduced in development product 0.4.8."
    },
    "connection": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "fresh",
        "stale",
        "unknown",
        "revoked"
      ]
    },
    "checks": {
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolMemberCheck"
      },
      "description": "The four convergence checks this host itself reported: pool-storage-reconciliation, pool-network-reconciliation, pool-media-reconciliation and pool-authority-replica. Empty while authoritative is false."
    },
    "access": {
      "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolMemberAccessCounts"
    },
    "failures": {
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolMemberFailure"
      },
      "description": "Per-member resource failures: the master's failed member_access rows, plus uplink rows derived from this member's own reported NICs against each pool VLAN, deduplicated against the master's failure for the same network."
    },
    "join": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolJoinStatus"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "This member's own reported inventory.managed.join, or null when it reports none."
    },
    "replica": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolMemberReplica"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "null on the pool master's own row."
    },
    "maintenance": {
      "type": [
        "boolean",
        "null"
      ],
      "description": "The master's durable drain flag for this host. null whenever authoritative is false: unknown, never assumed false."
    },
    "maintenance_since": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "RFC3339 UTC since when this host has been drained; empty when it is not drained, or while authoritative is false."
    },
    "guests": {
      "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolMemberGuests"
    },
    "last_maintenance": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolMemberOperation"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The newest pool-maintenance operation this Controller holds for this member, or null. It is Controller-held operation history, not master-reported state, so it is present whether or not the master is fresh."
    },
    "transfer": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolTransferStatus"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "This host's own report of the master change or eject it is part of, with role source, target or ejected. null whenever the host is not reporting now: a participant whose row is null while connection is not fresh is unknown, not finished."
    },
    "transfer_supported": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "This member's own advertised pool-authority-transfer-v1, so a promotion or master change whose target could not perform one is not offered at all. A host that is not reporting keeps its last advertised list, as everywhere else."
    },
    "fence": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolMemberFence"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "What the master's membership records about how this host would be excluded. null while the master is not fresh, and null when no profile is recorded."
    },
    "restricted": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PoolRestrictedStatus"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "This host's own Core-enforced refusal to act on pool authority. It is the host's own report, so it is shown whenever that host is fresh, whatever the pool master is doing \u2014 a restricted old master is precisely a host reporting for itself in a pool whose master changed. null when the host is not fresh or reports no restriction."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "host_id",
    "name",
    "role",
    "status",
    "error",
    "peer_origin",
    "joined_at",
    "connection",
    "checks",
    "access",
    "failures",
    "join",
    "replica",
    "maintenance",
    "maintenance_since",
    "guests",
    "last_maintenance",
    "transfer",
    "transfer_supported",
    "fence",
    "restricted"
  ]
}
PoolMemberCheck
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "pool-storage-reconciliation",
        "pool-network-reconciliation",
        "pool-media-reconciliation",
        "pool-authority-replica",
        "pool-restricted",
        "pool-promotion",
        "pool-authority-transfer"
      ],
      "description": "A fixed list in a fixed order. A check the host does not report is projected as unknown, never omitted, so the column cannot silently lose a row; new checks are appended and existing positions do not move. The list is the host's own report, so it is present exactly while that host is fresh, whatever the pool master is doing."
    },
    "status": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "healthy",
        "failed",
        "unknown"
      ]
    },
    "detail": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "name",
    "status",
    "detail"
  ]
}
PoolMemberAccessCounts
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "healthy": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0
    },
    "pending": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "Pool resources for which this member has reported no access row yet."

    "failed": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0
    },
    "stale": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "Access rows whose observation is older than the staleness bound."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "healthy",
    "pending",
    "failed",
    "stale"
  ],
  "description": "Counts of the master's member_access rows for this host across pool storage, networks and media. The master's own row carries no counts: member_access is the master's record about its members."
}

  ]

PoolRequest
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "request_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "pool_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "host_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "action": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "invite",
        "promotion-preflight",
        "bmc-probe"
      ]
    },
    "member_host_id": {

VMMemory
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "dedicated",
        "maximum"
      ],
      "description": "dedicated preallocates and locks the ceiling in host RAM while running: memory and currentMemory at size_mib, no balloon, and memoryBacking with immediate allocation, locked and nosharepages. Stopped VMs release physical RAM but retain their Nex capacity commitment. QEMU overhead is locked too. Requires updated Core; existing VMs need full shutdown, a successful stopped vm-update save and start. Legacy dedicated live edits fail before device effects with a stop-and-save instruction. Upgrade, autostart or guest reboot alone does not rewrite old definitions. maximum caps without reserving: the same ceiling plus a virtio balloon with free page reporting, so the guest returns pages it frees. Reclaim requires the balloon driver running in the guest (built into Linux; virtio-win guest tools on Windows); without it the guest drifts to the ceiling and holds it. There is no pressure-driven reclaim daemon."
    },
    "size_mib": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 512,
      "maximum": 262144,
      "description": "Memory ceiling in MiB. Both sides require at least 512; Controller caps the request at 262144."

    "size_mib"

}

VMNIC
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "network_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "Registered network that has succeeded on this VM's host and pool, resolved by resource ID."
    },
    "model": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "virtio",
        "e1000",
        "e1000e",
        "rtl8139",
        "vmxnet3"
      ],
      "description": "Which network card the guest sees. virtio is paravirtualised: fastest and lowest host CPU, but the guest needs a driver (built into Linux, virtio-win on Windows). e1000 and e1000e emulate Intel gigabit cards nearly every OS already drives, for guests and installers that cannot see a virtio adapter, at higher host CPU. rtl8139 emulates a 100 Mbit card for guests too old for a gigabit driver; the limit is the emulated hardware. vmxnet3 is VMware's paravirtualised adapter, for guests already carrying VMware drivers."
    },
    "mac": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^(([0-9a-f][02468ace])(:[0-9a-f]{2}){5})?$",
      "description": "Empty derives a stable MAC from the VM ID and the interface index (protocol.DerivedMAC: the 52:54:00 locally administered prefix, two octets of sha256(id) and the index), which never collides across a VM's at most 8 interfaces. A manual address must be six octets in canonical lower-case colon form and unicast; the pattern encodes the cleared multicast bit as an even second hex digit. All-zero addresses are refused, addresses are unique within the VM, and Controller additionally enforces uniqueness across the pool by plain string comparison. The VM list reports the effective address, and an edit freezes every automatic address into the definition (drawn from the VM's derived range above the highest index the VM uses, or the lowest free index when none above is free), so interfaces keep their identity across later edits."
    },
    "mtu": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1280,
      "maximum": 9216,
      "description": "Interface MTU, or 0 for the network's own. Accepted only when model is virtio: QEMU communicates an MTU to the guest through virtio's host_mtu feature and libvirt sizes the host tap to match, while the emulated models have no equivalent and would leave the guest on its own default. A value on any other model is refused rather than silently applied to the host side only. The floor is the IPv6 minimum MTU and the ceiling the largest jumbo frame common NICs accept; every device along the path must agree or traffic is dropped without an error."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "network_id",
    "model",
    "mac"
  ],
  "x-go-type": "protocol.VMNIC",
  "description": "One virtual network interface on a registered pool network. A VM may have none and at most 8."
}

      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^([a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,31})?$",
      "description": "Empty selects Core's default machine type (q35)."
    },
    "media_boot_order": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "0 keeps the CD drive out of the boot order; any other value joins the disks' contiguous 1..N numbering. Every VM has the drive, so the order is kept while it is empty and an ISO can be ejected from a running guest."
    },
    "secure_boot": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "",
        "on",
        "off"
      ],
      "description": "UEFI Secure Boot. Omitted means on with the Microsoft keys enrolled, which is exactly what libvirt already selected for every UEFI VM defined before this field existed, so a definition re-sent unchanged keeps the firmware its guest was installed with. off selects the plain OVMF build with no enrolled keys, for unsigned boot media or drivers. Requires uefi; on with bios is rejected. Core refuses the VM when the host's domain capabilities do not offer a matching firmware build, naming the setting rather than passing libvirt's firmware-selection error through. Changing it requires the VM to be shut off."
    },
    "tpm": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "",
        "none",
        "2.0"
      ],
      "description": "Emulated TPM. 2.0 adds a tpm-crb device backed by swtpm; omitted and none add no device, so a definition written before this field keeps exactly the devices it had. Windows 11 requires a TPM and refuses to install without one. Core refuses the VM when the host's domain capabilities do not advertise the emulator backend, rather than defining a device that cannot start. Changing it requires the VM to be shut off, and REMOVING a TPM is refused outright at any time: anything the guest sealed to it, including a Windows BitLocker key, would be lost, and libvirt cleans TPM state by iterating the devices the persistent definition still carries, so a redefine without it would orphan that state."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "firmware",
    "machine",
    "media_boot_order"
  ],
  "x-go-type": "protocol.VMBoot",
  "description": "Firmware, Secure Boot, TPM, machine type and the install media's place in the boot order. Boot order is per device (libvirt forbids mixing per-device boot with an os/boot device list), so at least one disk or the install media must carry a non-zero order."
}
VMCreateSpec
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Controller-assigned stable UUID; identity is preserved across Controller replacement and later migration."
    },
    "pool_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "host_id": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[^/\\u0000-\\u001f\\u007f-\\u009f\\ufffe\\uffff]+$",
      "description": "Nonblank VM name, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes (the byte limit is additionally enforced by Controller and Core). Spaces, case, dots, punctuation and Unicode are preserved exactly. Slashes, control characters and XML-invalid U+FFFE/U+FFFF are rejected. Core checks uniqueness on the host, journals the name and reports it for Controller adoption; failed or uncertain creations retain their reservation. Upgrade Controller and Core together to use the expanded naming syntax.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "maxLength": 200
    },
    "description": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 4096,
      "description": "Free-text operator note, at most 4096 characters."
    },
    "guest_os": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "",
        "linux",
        "windows",
        "other"
      ],
      "description": "Guest OS hint recorded for display and guest-tools advice; empty leaves it unset. It installs nothing and does not change the VM devices: disk bus and NIC model are chosen per device."
    },
    "cpu": {
      "$ref": "#/components/schemas/VMCPU"
    },
    "memory": {
      "$ref": "#/components/schemas/VMMemory"
    },
    "disks": {
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/components/schemas/VMDisk"
      },
      "minItems": 1,
      "maxItems": 8,
      "description": "One to eight disks; names unique within the VM."
    },
    "nics": {
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/components/schemas/VMNIC"
      },
      "maxItems": 8,
      "description": "Zero to eight network interfaces."
    },
    "boot": {
      "$ref": "#/components/schemas/VMBoot"
    },
    "media_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Install ISO (Media.id), empty for none. The ISO must be imported and verified on the placement host; it may live on any storage that host can read and does not need to share a repository with the VM's disks. Every VM has the CD drive, so a non-zero boot.media_boot_order does not require media_id: an emptied drive keeps its place in the boot order."
    },
    "drivers_media_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "ISO in the VM's second CD drive, for a driver disc an installer needs alongside its install media - a Windows guest installing to a VirtIO disk needs the virtio-win ISO here. Empty leaves that drive empty; the drive itself always exists on a host reporting vm-media-drivers-drive-v1. Must differ from media_id."
    },
    "start_after_create": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Honoured by the host inside the creation, after the definition is verified, so the creation itself has succeeded whether or not the flag is set: Core starts the guest exactly once and records the outcome in the journal entry's start field. A failed automatic start leaves the VM defined and stopped as a normal managed VM (power, console and media work; a replacement Controller adopts it) and is reported by the host as its own outcome with ID <operation-id>:start, kind vm-power, status failed and error 'VM created but not started: <reason>', which Controller records in Task history. A creation interrupted at the start step reconciles by observing libvirt: running means started, otherwise that outcome reads 'interrupted before the automatic start completed'. A failed or uncertain creation never boots. Controller issues no follow-on power request. Must be false in an edit."
    },
    "autostart": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "libvirt autostart, set while the stopped guest is defined so the host starts this VM on boot. It is not a start."
    },
    "tags": {
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "type": "string",
        "pattern": "^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$"
      },
      "maxItems": 16,
      "description": "Operator labels kept with the VM definition: each 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, at most 16. Controller sorts and de-duplicates them before validation; an invalid tag is 400 naming it (tag \"<tag>\" must be 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens), more than 16 distinct tags is 400 (a VM allows at most 16 tags). Tags are part of the complete definition, so an edit that omits them clears them. Nonempty tags need vm-tags-v1 on both the VM's host and its pool master, because an older Core would drop them: 409 \"the VM's host or its pool master does not support VM tags; upgrade Nex Core\" on updateVM and \"the selected host or its pool master does not support VM tags; upgrade Nex Core\" on createVM, after the replay check. Core journals them with the definition, the pool master keeps them in its pool VM record, and a fresh Controller adopts them from the host's reported definition. Omitted when empty and from older Core. They change no guest device and apply to a running VM. Introduced in development product 0.4.8."
    },
    "revision": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "Definition revision: 0 at creation, current + 1 for each edit. Core refuses any other value, so a stale edit after Controller replacement fails instead of applying an old definition. Reported back in Inventory.managed.vms with the current definition."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "id",
    "pool_id",
    "host_id",
    "name",
    "description",
    "guest_os",
    "cpu",
    "memory",
    "disks",
    "nics",
    "boot",
    "media_id",
    "start_after_create",
    "autostart",
    "revision"
  ],
  "x-go-type": "protocol.VMCreateSpec",
  "description": "The complete VM specification: Controller-assigned UUID and pool membership with separate host assignment, identity, CPU, memory, every disk and network interface, boot and install media, and the two lifecycle switches. Creation defines a stopped VM and never boots it. Dependencies must have succeeded on this host and pool. Both sides validate the shared bounds through protocol.ValidateVMSpec; Controller owns identity, reference existence, pool-wide MAC uniqueness and capacity."
}

  "x-go-type": "protocol.ManagedState",
  "description": "Every succeeded registration and VM definition from the Core managed journal, plus the host's appliance deployments, queued work and terminal outcomes; at most 10000 entries per resource list and 30000 outcomes; each list is omitted when empty. Pool, host and resource IDs inside entries are host-owned and stable across Controllers: a host's self-registered default entry carries its pool ID when the host knows it (hosts enrolled with host-owned identity), otherwise its host ID as a placeholder until adoption. Adoption records each entry under the host's current pool and host, which is a no-op for hosts that presented their own identity at enrollment; that is how a replaced Controller recovers a pool from its master. Entries the Controller already holds under the same ID and kind are silently current. Any other entry it cannot adopt (invalid, conflicting ID/path/source/name, references not adopted on the host, or missing from libvirt) is recorded once per host and entry as a needs_attention operation (request_id adopt-attention:<host>:<kind>:<id>, actor system, error prefixed 'not adopted from host report:') with an audit entry adopt.attention naming the reason; the record is marked succeeded once the entry is adopted. A vm-create entry interrupted after its definition step is re-observed by the host on report and promoted to succeeded when the persistent domain matches its journaled definition."

PoolMemberReplica
{
  "type": "object",
  "description": "One member's authority replica as the two hosts that report it describe it: the member says what it holds, the master says what it last saw acknowledged. Neither number is derived, stored or reconciled by the Controller, and no host reports an absolute pool authority generation, so there is no third number to compare against. null on the pool master's own row: the master holds the authority, not a replica of it.",
  "properties": {
    "generation": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "The member's own report; 0 when it holds none or is not fresh."
    },
    "digest": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "verified": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "The member proved the replica against the pool CA it holds."
    },
    "received_at": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "RFC3339 UTC, or empty."
    },
    "acknowledged_generation": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "What the master last observed this member acknowledge; 0 when the master is not fresh or the member never acknowledged one."
    },
    "acknowledged_at": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "RFC3339 UTC, or empty."
    },
    "error": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The master's reason for this member when it has one, otherwise the member's own reported reason."
    },
    "state": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "unknown",
        "unsupported",
        "refused",
        "awaiting",
        "unverified",
        "unknown",
        "behind",
        "current"
      ],
      "description": "First match wins, in this order: unknown when the master is not fresh or this member is not fresh (a replica that was current an hour ago is not current now, and freshness deliberately outranks capability, because a stale host's capability list is a memory too); unsupported when the master or this member does not advertise pool-authority-replica-v2; refused when either side reports an error; awaiting when both generations are 0; unverified when the member holds a replica it has not proven; behind when the two generations disagree, the pool master reports an authority generation one of them is below, or another fresh member of this pool is acknowledged at a strictly higher generation; current otherwise. behind with generation above acknowledged_generation means the master's observation lags, not the member: both numbers are shown because the single word cannot say which side is stale. The pool master's reported authority generation is the absolute reference this ladder gained with the master change slice; the peer comparison stays, because the master's authority record can itself be an older report than a member's. When authority is null the ladder behaves exactly as it did before. PoolTransferStatus
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "operation_id": {

      "description": "The Controller operation that started the transfer, or the identifier the transfer was recorded under."
    },
    "action": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "promote or eject: Core's own name for what this transfer does. A fence-verified promotion of a surviving member is also promote, and is told apart by role: candidate. The Controller's requested action (master-change, eject, transfer-cancel) is reported separately in last_transfer."
    },
    "role": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "This host's part in the transfer: source is the pool master that started it, target is the host taking the authority, ejected is the host leaving the pool, candidate is the surviving member running a fence-verified promotion."
    },
    "target_host_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The transfer's subject: the host becoming master, or the host being ejected."
    },
    "stage": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The stage this host has durably reached. For a master change: freeze, replicate, activate (the signed hand-off), repoint (every other host is told, in the new master's own signed words, who the master is now). For an eject: freeze, remove (the durable membership change, after which nothing stays frozen), repoint, leave. For a promotion: preflight, fence, activate, optional catalog-rebuild (after authority commit when repositories exist and the signed catalog is empty), repoint. A catalog import error leaves catalog-rebuild at needs_attention for retry before repoint, without reactivating or rolling back the committed master. done and aborted are terminal."
    },
    "status": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "pending while the hosts are still running it; needs_attention means durable and still running, not an error.",
      "enum": [
        "pending",
        "succeeded",
        "failed",
        "needs_attention"
      ]
    },
    "error": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "This host's own last refusal or failure, bounded and sanitized."
    },
    "authority_generation": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "The pool authority generation this transfer is pinned to."
    },
    "frozen": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "True while this host is refusing pool authority writes for the transfer. Running guests are unaffected and stop is never refused."
    },
    "cancellable": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Core's own answer to \"may this still be cancelled?\", so no caller has to infer it from stage names. True only before the transfer's first irreversible durable step: a master change until the pool-CA-signed hand-off, an eject until the membership without that member is written, and never for a promotion, which fences. It is computed from the same predicate the cancel itself is gated on, so the reported flag and the accepted cancel cannot drift. It is always present: a caller reads one field for every kind of transfer and never has to tell \"not cancellable\" from \"not reported\"."
    },
    "handed_off": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "The outgoing master's own durable answer to \"have I signed this pool's authority away?\", reported rather than inferred from stage names or refusal sentences. Only the source records it, so a target or ejected host always reports false. It is always present, so an older Core that omits it is distinguishable from one that reports false."
    },
    "observed_at": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date-time",
      "description": "When this host wrote this report."
    },
    "automatic": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "True only when Core initiated this promotion automatically through the supported two-host BMC path. Omitted for manual promotions and by older Core versions. This is reported metadata, not a fence proof. Automatic promotion requires Host fencing enabled; storage-lease and witness-based promotion paths are not implemented; qdevice registration and status do not produce fence proof."
    }
  },

    "operation_id",
    "action",
    "role",

    "status",
    "cancellable",
    "handed_off",

PoolFenceProfileRequest
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "request_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Stable, operator-supplied idempotency key. The stored replay payload is the profile as sent, without the credential and without the reference Core allocates, so an exact retry stays byte-identical."
    },
    "fence": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/StorageClusterFence"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The profile to record; null clears it. redfish and ipmilan take {endpoint, target_id, username}; virsh takes the pinned SSH fields. A client never supplies tls_fingerprint: for a redfish profile Core connects when it records it, captures the certificate the controller presents, writes that fingerprint into the profile itself and proves over that pinned connection that the controller manages this host's machine before recording anything. Before any power-off Core asks the management controller which machine it manages \u2014 the Redfish ComputerSystem.UUID, compared exactly, or IPMI Get System GUID, where either documented byte order counts \u2014 and compares it with the target host's own SMBIOS system UUID in the master's membership record. A mismatch, a host with no unique hardware identity and an unreadable controller each refuse the fence and power nothing off. Redirects are never followed, so the identity cannot be read from one machine while another is powered off. Core refuses a BMC profile whose host reports no unique hardware identity or which names no username, and refuses SCSI-PR outright. A refused profile's delivered password is released from the master's credential store."
    },
    "credential": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/StorageCredentials"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Optional material for the profile, never stored by the Controller. It is delivered over the existing one-time encrypted credential handoff, Core allocates its own private reference, and only that opaque reference is written into the command. Nothing reaches SQLite, the audit trail, the response or any log. A virsh profile takes {ssh_private_key, ssh_known_hosts}; redfish and ipmilan take {secret}, the password of the account named in the profile; a scsi_pr profile takes none. Omitting it means the profile must already name a credential_ref Core knows."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "request_id",
    "fence"
  ],
  "description": "Record or clear how a member of this pool would be power-fenced. Unknown fields are refused."
}

      "format": "date-time",
      "description": "The host's own clock when it started feeding this device, carried over unchanged while it goes on feeding the same one. Nothing compares it with another host's clock. It exists so that a host which stopped and started its watchdog \u2014 a reboot, a cluster restart \u2014 produces a record that differs from the one before it: an identical record is never written and never replicated, and a survivor would otherwise be unable to tell \"armed since before it left\" from \"was armed once, and has been up unarmed since\". A survivor refuses a watchdog proof against a target that rejoined its Corosync partition after the last armed record it holds."
    }

    "armed",
    "armed_at",
    "observed_at"
  ],
  "x-go-type": "protocol.PoolWatchdogArmed",
  "description": "A host's own report that it has armed its watchdog, kept in the pool master's durable membership and replicated. It is the first of the three conditions of a watchdog exclusion proof, and the host that has to read it is a promotion candidate whose master has gone, which is why it is durable rather than an observation."
}

PoolFenceCluster
{
  "type": "object",
  "description": "The master's memory-only pool cluster observation. Pools of three to five ready hosts can form the watchdog cluster when Host fencing is on and no clustered-storage repository is configured. An eligible two-host pool instead can register Controller-hosted qnetd and configure Corosync qdevice; the reported forming/degraded status reflects qdevice state, but no two-host SBD arming or witness-loss exclusion proof is enabled. Durable witness selection and CA pin are in PoolMembership.witness; native readiness is rechecked after restart.",
  "properties": {
    "state": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "off",
        "not_available",
        "forming",
        "arming",
        "armed",
        "degraded"
      ],
      "description": "off is the pool's Host fencing setting. not_available means the pool has no applicable cluster or witness support. For the three-or-more-host watchdog cluster, forming waits for Corosync quorum, arming is the one-host-at-a-time rollout, and degraded means hosts are not all armed. In an eligible two-host pool, forming means qdevice is not verified and degraded can mean it is connected and voting; two-host watchdog arming remains withheld in either state."
    },
    "detail": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Core's own sentence for the state. A client shows it as written."
    },
    "armed": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "How many hosts of this pool's cluster are feeding a watchdog."
    },
    "total": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "How many hosts are in this pool's cluster. Every ready host that is not in maintenance is in it: a host is never silently left out of the quorum the rest of the pool makes its decisions with."
    },
    "arming_host_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The host whose turn it is to arm, by host ID. Arming means restarting that host's cluster services, so exactly one host in a pool does it at a time, and whose turn it is is derived from the membership rather than granted. A host that cannot arm holds the turn and the rollout stops there with that host's own reason, which is the safe direction: fewer armed hosts is less protection, never a false proof."
    }
  },
  "required": [

    "armed",
    "total"
